# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 108 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 52 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_108_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 108

**1** Jesus said: "Whoever drinks from my mouth will become like me.

**2** I myself shall become that person,

**3** and the hidden things will be revealed to him."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** One of the most theologically profound sayings in Thomas. Three movements: (1) Drinking from Jesus's mouth leads to becoming like Jesus (disciple transformed). (2) Jesus becoming that person (Jesus transformed into the disciple — mutual *henosis*). (3) The hidden things revealed (the consequence of union = disclosure of mysteries).

**"Drinks from my mouth"** — *pashej ebo lpamou*: the mouth as source of living teaching/water. Cf. John 7:37 ("let him come to me and drink") but Thomas's version is mutual and more intimate.

**"I myself shall become that person"** — the reciprocal transformation is without parallel in any canonical text. It suggests that the mystical union changes both parties.

**"The hidden things"** — *apokrupha*: the mysteries of the cosmos and self that are inaccessible without this union. No Synoptic parallel exists.
